buildings.reason: the GeoJSON ingest reads Polygon/MultiPolygon footprints and retains only the centroid and the area (PowerGridGraph.extract_building_centers_and_areas); the polygons are not carried into the base snapshot, and nothing downstream of it can reconstruct them -- a consumer that wants footprints must go back to the source layer

measured.absent_reason: this instance carries no measured observations; the SDK ships the ingest path, not measured data -- place tidy measurement exports and the declared entity_join in the observations directory named here to feed a deployment's own AMI/SCADA data through gridalyn.twin.observation.ingest, which is what makes a deployment a digital shadow rather than a model

projects.description: EV hosting capacity and flexibility across a 540-transformer distribution fleet, with the transformer rating convention as a declared axis.

experiments.objective: Classify every pole transformer in the fleet at each adoption level and adoption-clustering level, under both rating conventions: never binds / flexibility defers it / needs steel / constrained by the winter heating base. This is the study's primary result; the per-feeder stages below are the worked example behind it.
Measure the firm EV hosting limit (first line/transformer overload) on the radial feeder without flexibility contracts. Extended with the flexible case and hosting-expansion headline in Phases 9-10.

projects.label: Ev Hosting Flex
projects.objective:
Determine, across the whole pole-transformer fleet, how many assets bind as EV adoption grows from today (0.11 EV/home) to Québec saturation (1.32 EV/home, every household light vehicle electrified), how many a flexibility contract defers, and how many need reinforcement regardless.
The unit of analysis is the FLEET, not one feeder. Measured on this network, the median asset and the tail answer differently: the governed 6-home unit hosts full saturation firmly, while a share of the 540 binds well before it. A single-feeder headline reports whichever of those the chosen feeder happens to be.
The transformer rating is a declared axis, not an assumption. Judging a winter peak against a nameplate defined at a 30 °C ambient breaks the coupling between load and thermal capability — in a heating-dominated feeder both are driven by the same outdoor temperature and rise together. On this network that choice moves more assets than the entire EV transition does, so both conventions are emitted.
